newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission likely to adopt landfill waste proposal.
newsitem.headline: Commission likely to adopt landfill waste proposal.

text.p: The European Commission, barring any last-minute hitches, is likely to adopt on Wednesday its draft proposal for a directive setting rules for landfill waste dumps, a Commission official said on Tuesday.

Environment Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard has seen repeated delays for a proposal intended to replace the text, based on COM(93)275, that was thrown out by the European Parliament in May last year amid complaints about planned derogations.

The original draft aimed to harmonise rules governing landfill waste dumps in the EU, setting technical and environmental norms for their operation, classifying different types of wastes and determining the procedures for accepting waste for dumping.

The replacement proposal has run into problems in recent weeks first with Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan, because of planned limits on the organic content of landfill waste, and recently due to reservations, expressed by Energy Commissioner Christos Papoutsis, about limits on small-island derogations.
These are thought unlikely to derail the proposal this time around, the official said.
